land.text: the whole Ukrainian SSR: 'outright independence was proclaimed on 24 August 1991'

predecessors.note: The Ukrainian SSR dossier ends in August 1991 and names ukraine as successor; the Soviet Union itself ended on 26 December 1991.

correction.text: the 1992 outline used for the months of independence in 1991 (24 August 1991, confirmed by the referendum of 1 December 1991)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Ukraine shape begins in 1992 although independence was proclaimed on 24 August 1991. Same outline; a hand-over year with the Ukrainian SSR dossier (ends August 1991).

590,177 km2 for 1992-2023 against the infobox 603,628 km2 (the body says 603,550 km2; ratio 0.98). The shape keeps Crimea as Ukrainian land throughout, which is the de jure position (UNGA 68/262): Russia's occupation from February 2014 and the Donbas republics from April 2014 are ledger events drawn over it. The infobox does not say whether its figure includes Crimea. From 2014 the ledger takes the Donbas lands away (losses to the two republics); the 2024 keyframe restates the shape without them.

minus.text: the 1992 outline, including Crimea (Ukraine's territory within its internationally recognised borders, 603,628 km2 in the infobox)

union.text: the Donetsk People's Republic with its 2022 gains, about 55-60% of Donetsk Oblast, lost to the republic in 2014-2015 and 2022 and annexed by Russia on 30 September 2022
Luhansk Oblast, lost to the Luhansk People's Republic in 2014 and 2022 and annexed by Russia on 30 September 2022

minus.text: the Donbas land that left Ukraine's control for the two republics and then Russia

correction.text: the 1992 outline, including Crimea, minus the Donbas lands the ledger loses to the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics (the 2014 and 2015 losses and the 2022 losses to the republics), which Russia annexed on 30 September 2022 and the republics' dossiers dissolve into russian-federation; Crimea and the occupied south stay in Ukraine's shape as Russian occupation (hatched), because they were never given to a separate state

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 2024 shape is 568,320 km2, exactly 21,857 km2 smaller than 1992-2023 - Crimea, the same piece it adds to Russia in 2014 - and so changes in 2024 for no event. Ukraine's own page says the regions include 'Sevastopol and the Autonomous Republic of Crimea that were annexed by the Russian Federation in 2014'. The outline therefore stays whole and the occupations are drawn by the ledger ('Russian troops controlled about 17% of Ukraine's internationally recognised territory' a year after February 2022; roughly 20% on the war page). Revised after review: the earlier correction was the whole 1992 outline, which contradicted the ledger (the Donbas losses of 2014, 2015 and 2022 were never given back), so the 2024 frame would have returned the Donbas to Ukraine's solid. The shape now subtracts the Donbas lands and so agrees with russian-federation's 2024 keyframe (the 2013 outline plus the same two lands). The reviewer's alternative (retype the Donbas losses as occupation) was not taken because it would leave the republics' founding, gain and dissolve events in their own dossiers (eu-22-x) without a mirror.

region.text: Ukraine within its Soviet-republic borders

ledger.note: 24 August 1991: Ukraine proclaims independence. 'outright independence was proclaimed on 24 August 1991'; 'approved by 92% of the Ukrainian electorate in a referendum on 1 December'; the Soviet Union 'formally voted itself out of existence on 26 December'. In 1994 Ukraine gave up nuclear weapons in the Budapest memorandum for guarantees of 'security and territorial integrity'.

region.text: Crimea and Sevastopol, 'the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and Sevastopol' in Ukrainian terms

ledger.note: 27 February 2014: Russia seizes Crimea. 'On 27 February, Russian special forces without insignia seized strategic sites across Crimea'; Russia 'formally incorporated Crimea on 18 March 2014'; Ukraine calls it the 'temporary occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and Sevastopol by Russia'; UNGA 68/262 (27 March 2014) affirmed Ukraine's territorial integrity. Owner's record of the occupation shown in russian-federation.

region.text: the Donbas, where 'demonstrations by pro-Russian, separatist, and counter-revolutionary groups took place' from late February 2014

ledger.note: April 2014: the war in the Donbas begins. Pro-Russian activists seized the Donetsk government headquarters on 6 April and proclaimed the republic 'the next day'; 'On 12 April 2014, a heavily armed paramilitary unit crossed the border from Russia into Ukraine'. The page's sentence on the 12 April takeover is cut short, so the town is not named here.

region.text: the Donbas, where 'demonstrations by pro-Russian, separatist, and counter-revolutionary groups took place' from late February 2014

ledger.note: 29 April 2014: Luhansk's government seat falls. 'On 29 April, armed pro-Russian activists stormed and occupied the Luhansk regional government headquarters.'

region.text: the separatist-held parts of Donetsk Oblast in April 2014: Donetsk and Horlivka, Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, and Mariupol (the DPR dossier's founding region)

ledger.note: April 2014: separatists take the area around Donetsk. The page dates the seizure of the Donetsk headquarters (6 April) and the proclamation of the republic the next day; the extent is the DPR dossier's reading. Revised after review: the region now includes Kramatorsk (45 km) and Mariupol (35 km), as in donetsk-people-s-republic /ledger/0; both were retaken within weeks (the next two events). The War in Donbas page: 'On 12 April 2014, a heavily-armed Russian paramilitary unit crossed the border from Russia into Ukraine' (Sloviansk), 'The same day as the capture of Sloviansk, Girkin's men attacked the police station in nearby Kramatorsk', and 'Between 12 and 14 April 2014, Russian militants took control of government buildings in several towns'; the page does not name Mariupol among them, so that part of the region is the DPR dossier's reading.

region.text: the area around Luhansk, Alchevsk and Stakhanov held by the separatists (the LPR dossier's 2014 reading)

ledger.note: April 2014: separatists take the area around Luhansk after the 29 April storming of the regional government headquarters; the extent is the LPR dossier's reading.

region.text: Mariupol, retaken by Ukraine

ledger.note: 13 June 2014: Ukraine retakes Mariupol. 'On 13 June, Ukrainian troops and the National Guard retook the city of Mariupol' (War in Donbas page). Mirrors donetsk-people-s-republic /ledger/2.

region.text: Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, retaken by Ukraine

ledger.note: 5 July 2014: Ukraine retakes Sloviansk and Kramatorsk. 'In a further blow to the insurgents, government forces retook the stronghold of Sloviansk on 5 July'; 'Sporadic fighting continued until 5 July, when the insurgents withdrew from Kramatorsk.' Mirrors donetsk-people-s-republic /ledger/3.

region.text: Debaltseve and its salient

ledger.note: February 2015: Ukraine retreats from Debaltseve. 'By 18 February 2015, the 8,000 Ukrainian troops were close to surrounded and had been forced to retreat from Debaltseve', days after Minsk II.

region.text: the Donbas, where 'demonstrations by pro-Russian, separatist, and counter-revolutionary groups took place' from late February 2014

ledger.note: 12 February 2015: Minsk II. 'A new package of measures to end the conflict, known as Minsk II, was agreed on 12 February 2015'; the line of contact then holds until February 2022 (Minsk I, 5 September 2014, had drawn an earlier 'line of demarcation').

region.text: the Donbas, where 'demonstrations by pro-Russian, separatist, and counter-revolutionary groups took place' from late February 2014

ledger.note: 12 February 2015: Minsk II ends the open fighting in Luhansk as in Donetsk.

region.text: 'almost all of Kherson Oblast, and about 70% of Zaporizhzhia Oblast' held by Russia at annexation

ledger.note: February 2022 onward: Russia occupies the south. The full-scale invasion began on 24 February 2022 (war page); the annexation page gives the holdings at 30 September 2022 but not the capture dates. The whole-oblast region over-states Zaporizhzhia (about 70%). Owner's record of Russia's occupation.

region.text: Donetsk Oblast

ledger.note: 24 February 2022: the full-scale invasion reopens the Donbas front. 'On 21 February 2022, Russia recognised the independence of the DPR and LPR' and 'on 24 February 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion of the entire country of Ukraine' (Donetsk People's Republic page). Mirrors donetsk-people-s-republic /ledger/6.

region.text: Luhansk Oblast

ledger.note: 24 February 2022: the full-scale invasion reopens the Luhansk front. 'On 21 February 2022, Russia recognised the LPR and DPR as sovereign states' and 'Three days later, on 24 February 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion of the entire country of Ukraine' (Luhansk People's Republic page). Mirrors luhansk-people-s-republic /ledger/3.

region.text: the places Russian forces captured north of Kyiv in February-March 2022: Chernobyl and Pripyat, Bucha, Hostomel, Vorzel, half of Irpin, and Trostianets in Sumy Oblast

ledger.note: 24 February 2022: Russian forces cross into Kyiv, Chernihiv, Sumy and Zhytomyr oblasts. 'On 24 February 2022 ... the Russian military crossed the' border 'entering the oblasts (regions) of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Sumy, and Zhytomyr'; they 'captured the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant and the ghost city of Pripyat', Trostianets 'was occupied by a garrison of Russian troops on 1 March', 'capturing Bucha, Hostomel, and Vorzel by 5 March' and 'half of Irpin by 14 March'. Kyiv, Chernihiv (encircled 10 March) and Sumy were never taken and the page outlines no front line, so the region is circles at the places it says were captured (the researcher's reading, not whole oblasts). Owner's record of Russia's occupation (mirrors russian-federation).

region.text: the east of Kharkiv Oblast held by Russia from late February 2022: Shevchenkove, Kupiansk, Balakliia, Izium and Vovchansk and their surroundings

ledger.note: 26 February 2022 onward: Russian forces occupy the east of Kharkiv Oblast. 'Shevchenkove came under Russian occupation on 26 February 2022', Kupiansk 'on 27 February', Balakliia 'on 2 March', and 'in early April, Russian forces captured Izium'; Russian forces also held Vovchansk. Kharkiv city was never taken. The region is circles at the named towns cut to the oblast (47 cells, about 11,900 km2, against the page's 'over 500 settlements and 12,000 square kilometers' retaken): the researcher's reading. Mirrors russian-federation.

region.text: the same places, evacuated by Russian forces

ledger.note: Late March - early April 2022: Russia withdraws from north of Kyiv. 'Russia withdrew its forces from Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Chernihiv and Sumy oblasts in late March and early April 2022, and Ukrainian forces retook control'; 'Ukrainian forces entered' Bucha 'on 1 April'; the infobox dates the campaign '24 February - 8 April 2022'. The war page: Russia 'abandoned an attempt to seize Kyiv in early April'. The month is the page's 'early April'. Mirrors russian-federation.

region.text: Mariupol

ledger.note: 20 May 2022: Mariupol falls. 'By 20 May, Mariupol fell to Russian troops following a prolonged siege.' Revised after review: the counterpart is the Donetsk People's Republic, whose June 2022 gain (donetsk-people-s-republic /ledger/7) holds Mariupol in its region, not russian-federation, which has no Mariupol gain. The DPR page, reopened, says only that 'the Russian Armed Forces laid siege to Mariupol for almost three months' and lists the Mariupol Urban District as Russian-controlled without a date, so the day is the war page's; the DPR dossier dates its 2022 gain to June, a month later, and its owner should split Mariupol out at May. (The earlier phrase 'with no territorial change' about the abandoned attempt on Kyiv was wrong: see the occupation north of Kyiv, February to April 2022.)

region.text: the Donetsk land Russian and DPR forces took in 2022 beyond the 2014-2015 line, without Mariupol (lost in May): to about 55% of the oblast

ledger.note: By June 2022: Russian and DPR forces hold about 55% of Donetsk Oblast. 'Around 55% of Donetsk Oblast came under the control of Russia and the DPR by June 2022' (Donetsk People's Republic page); the page gives the share, not the towns or the day, so the month is its 'by June' and the region is the DPR dossier's (donetsk-people-s-republic /ledger/7) minus Mariupol. Replaces the earlier September 2022 loss to russian-federation, which had no mirror there and counted the 2014 DPR area twice.

region.text: Sievierodonetsk and the Lysychansk area on the Siverskyi Donets

ledger.note: 25 June 2022: Sievierodonetsk falls. 'On 25 June 2022, Sievierodonetsk was fully occupied by Russian and separatist forces' (Luhansk People's Republic page). Mirrors luhansk-people-s-republic /ledger/4.

region.text: the rest of Luhansk Oblast

ledger.note: 3 July 2022: Lysychansk falls and all of Luhansk Oblast is held. 'This was followed by the capture of Lysychansk on 3 July, which brought all of Luhansk Oblast ... under the control of Russian and separatist forces' (Luhansk People's Republic page). Mirrors luhansk-people-s-republic /ledger/5.

region.text: the east of Kharkiv Oblast retaken by Ukraine in September 2022, as occupied from February

ledger.note: September 2022: Ukraine's Kharkiv counteroffensive ends the occupation. 'On 6 September 2022, the Armed Forces of Ukraine launched a major counteroffensive'; Balakliia and Shevchenkove were retaken the next day, 'on 10 September, Ukrainian forces retook Kupiansk and Izium', and by 13 September Ukraine had retaken 'all of Kharkiv Oblast west of the Oskil River'. The Russo-Ukrainian war page: 'recaptured the majority of Kharkiv Oblast in September'. Typed occupation_end (it was typed gain, for the whole oblast, before review) because the land was carried as occupation from February 2022 and Ukraine never lost it in this ledger; Russian forces kept the ground east of the Oskil. Mirrors russian-federation.

region.text: Donetsk Oblast

ledger.note: 30 September 2022: the republic ends in annexation. 'On 30 September 2022, Russia's president Vladimir Putin announced the annexation of the DPR' (Donetsk People's Republic page); the fighting for the rest of Donetsk Oblast continues as Ukraine against Russia (no event here: the pages opened give no later line). Mirrors donetsk-people-s-republic /ledger/8.

region.text: Luhansk Oblast

ledger.note: 30 September 2022: the republic ends in annexation. 'On 30 September 2022, Russia's president Vladimir Putin addressed the Russian parliament' and 'announced and signed the annexation of four regions' (Luhansk People's Republic page). Mirrors luhansk-people-s-republic /ledger/6.

region.text: the right bank of the Dnieper in Kherson Oblast, from which Russia withdrew: Kherson and its surroundings, Snihurivka, Beryslav, Davydiv Brid and Dudchany

ledger.note: 9-11 November 2022: Russia withdraws from Kherson and the right bank. 'On 9 November, Russian troops were ordered to withdraw from Kherson'; 'Russia announced the withdrawal of its troops from Kherson and the right bank of the Dnieper'; 'On 11 November, Ukrainian troops entered the city of Kherson'; the annexation page: 'including Kherson on 11 November 2022'. Typed occupation_end (it was typed gain before review) because the land is carried as occupation (the 2022-2 occupation of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia), so Ukraine never lost it. The region is circles at the right-bank towns the page names, cut to the oblast (28 cells, about 7,100 km2); Davydiv Brid and Dudchany had been retaken on 4 October, earlier than the withdrawal, and the event is dated at the withdrawal. The page gives no line, so the extent is the researcher's reading. Mirrors russian-federation.

region.text: the part of Kursk Oblast around Sudzha entered by Ukraine ('an area of up to 350 square kilometres'), a 15 km circle cut to the oblast

ledger.note: August 2024: Ukraine enters Russia's Kursk Oblast. 'In August 2024, the Ukrainian Armed Forces launched an incursion into Russia's Kursk Oblast', capturing 'an area of up to 350 square kilometres' (Ukrainian claim). Revised after review: the zone was the whole of Kursk Oblast (about 31,100 km2) and is now a 15 km circle around Sudzha cut to the oblast (3 cells, about 760 km2), the same zone as russian-federation /ledger/22; the Ukrainian incursion page (reopened) gives 'Oleshnya in the direction of Sudzha' as the aim and claims of 'over 1,000 km2' and '1,250 square kilometers' at the mid-August peak.

wars.name: Russo-Ukrainian war

zones.text: Crimea and Sevastopol, 'the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and Sevastopol' in Ukrainian terms
the Donbas, where 'demonstrations by pro-Russian, separatist, and counter-revolutionary groups took place' from late February 2014
the places north of Kyiv held from 24 February to early April 2022
east Kharkiv Oblast, held from February to September 2022
the Ukrainian foothold around Sudzha in Kursk Oblast, from 6 August 2024

wars.outcome: Russia took Crimea in 2014 and the Donbas republics held part of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts; after the invasion of 24 February 2022 Russia occupied 'roughly 20%' of Ukraine and proclaimed its annexation of four oblasts on 30 September 2022; Ukraine recovered Kharkiv Oblast (September 2022) and Kherson (11 November 2022). Ongoing at the end of the data.
wars.note: 'The Russo-Ukrainian war began in February 2014 and is ongoing.' Minsk I (5 September 2014) and Minsk II (12 February 2015) froze the Donbas line until 2022. Revised after review: zones added for the north of Kyiv, east Kharkiv Oblast and the (narrowed) Kursk foothold.

certainty.note: Ukraine's recognised borders follow the Soviet republic boundary. Exceptions: Crimea from 2014, the Donbas line of contact 2014-2022 and the southern and eastern fronts since 2022 are occupation or front lines (soft).

notes:
Ukraine, written by eu-22-g on 2026-11-01 from the Ukraine and Russo-Ukrainian war pages (two pages, the budget) plus two pages read for the russian-federation dossier.

Wikidata Q598570 is shared with sloboda-ukraine, but that is the Cossack-era region (dossier sloboda-ukraine, 1650-1765) and a different state; the two are not merged.

Cliopatria: the 1992-2023 shape is accepted; the 2024 shape (568,320 km2) drops exactly the 21,857 km2 that Russia's 2014 shape gains, i.e. Crimea, ten years late and for no event, so it is corrected to the whole outline. Crimea and the 2022 Russian holdings stay in Ukraine's shape and are drawn as Russian occupation (occupation_start events recorded from the owner's side, mirrored in russian-federation) in line with the project's scope; how Russia's annexation of the Donetsk and Luhansk parts is drawn is settled in the revision below.

Not on the pages opened: the dates of the Sievierodonetsk/Lysychansk, Kherson-city and Melitopol captures in 2022, the front lines of 2023-2024 (Bakhmut, Avdiivka, the 2023 counteroffensive were absent from the war summary page), the border treaties of the 1990s-2000s and the Black Sea Fleet / Crimea arrangements of 1997. Ukraine's presidents are listed on the page without term dates, so there is no ruler strip. Ongoing contests and occupations have no end event, so the validator warns about them.


Revision of 2026-11-01 (after the adversarial review; fixes applied from reopened pages). (1) Donbas treatment settled together with russian-federation: the Donbas lands are plain losses to the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics (2014, 2015 and 2022), which then dissolve into Russia, so the 2024 keyframe is the 1992 outline minus those lands and Russia's 2024 keyframe adds them; Crimea and the occupied south stay in Ukraine's shape as Russian occupation. (2) The old September 2022 loss of the Donbas to russian-federation (no mirror, and it counted the 2014 DPR area twice) is replaced by losses to the DPR (June 2022, about 55% of Donetsk Oblast, War page via the DPR page) and the LPR (Sievierodonetsk June, the rest of Luhansk Oblast July 2022), with the 2022 contest_start and contest_end for both republics, mirroring their dossiers; Mariupol (20 May 2022) now has the DPR as counterpart, and the DPR owner should split it out of its June gain. (3) The 2014 DPR loss now includes Kramatorsk and Mariupol, and the two June and July 2014 gains from the DPR are added. (4) Added the occupation north of Kyiv (24 February - early April 2022) and of east Kharkiv Oblast (26 February - September 2022), retyped the September Kharkiv and November Kherson events as occupation_end, widened Kherson to the right-bank towns on the 2022 Kherson counteroffensive page, and narrowed the Kursk zone to a 15 km circle at Sudzha. (5) Still open: the March 2025 end of the Kursk contest (Ukrainian incursion page: Sudzha retaken 13 March, Ukrainian withdrawal confirmed 16 March 2025), the front lines of 2023-2024, and the post-September 2022 Donetsk front (Ukraine against Russia, not an event here).
